signals.entity: ROPECO Bucuresti SRL (Romanian Business Consult group)
signals.signal: local-peer. ROPECO Bucuresti, part of the Romanian Business Consult group, is the authorised Romanian distributor for GLORY Global Solutions and also carries Ingenico EFT-POS terminals, HSM, Zebra, Honeywell, Sunmi, Wertheim and Promet safes. On 28/04/2026 ROPECO published that its general director Cristian Christodorescu was honoured at a GLORY EMEA Distributor event for 'over three decades' of partnership, confirming the Glory channel in Romania is held by ROPECO in 2026. Its own catalogue covers teller cash recyclers (TCR), Glory CASHINFINITY CI-100/CI-200 back-office cash management, self-service cash deposit (RCD 200), banknote counting/sorting/verification and coin rolling. No revenue, unit or bank-name figures are published and none are estimated here.
signals.implies: Printec's Glory/Sesami TCR and cash-recycler line is channel-blocked in Romania: Glory's EMEA distribution for the country sits with ROPECO, so a Glory-led branch cash-automation pitch to a Romanian bank will meet the vendor's own partner. Printec should lead Romania with NCR/Sesami recyclers and x-core plus managed field services rather than Glory, and treat ROPECO as the named incumbent to displace on branch TCR and self-service deposit deals.
signals.likelihood: High that ROPECO bids any Romanian branch cash-automation or self-service-deposit opportunity Printec pursues in the next 6-12 months
signals.followup: Establish through NCR/Sesami whether Printec has a competing recycler line it can lead with in Romania, and map ROPECO's installed bank base (its shop site names only retail references).

signals.signal: local-peer, and the strongest genuinely-new Romanian cash-automation rival this run. Eutron describes itself as the only Romanian company covering the full cash-flow-management and cash-processing chain, with a distribution and service network covering 100% of Romanian territory through 18 service centres and 26+ years of trading. Portfolio spans automatic banknote recycling machines for front and back office (collection, counting, authentication, storage and dispensing - i.e. TCR-class kit), RIBAO BCS-160 sorter and BC-40 multi-currency counters, Gunnebo safes and vaults, Oberthur Cash Protection CIT security, queue management, people counting and digital signage. Its own site records a delivered 'Office Digital Self Check-In' kiosk project in the reception areas of Alpha Bank Romania head offices. Trigger: fourteen below-threshold DIRECT awards published 04/08/2026-25/08/2026 by DGRFP Cluj-Napoca (CIF 4426336), every one to Eutron, totalling RON 25,463.94, CPV 50311400-2, for repair and servicing of RIBAO BCS 160 banknote counters at named State Treasury offices (notices DAN2823746, DAN2823769, DAN2824267, DAN2824281, DAN2824300, DAN2829821, DAN2829828, DAN2832656, DAN2832671, DAN2832998, DAN2833103, DAN2839343, DAN2839374, DAN2839421).
signals.source_name: eutron.ro (company site) + e-licitatie.ro direct-acquisition notices (via Agent 2 sweep 27/08/2026)
signals.implies: Eutron is a head-on competitor to Printec's cash automation/recycler line, its physical-security line and its self-service kiosk line, and it already sits inside a Printec footprint reference account (Alpha Bank) on the kiosk side. Its 18-centre nationwide service network is exactly the managed/field-services differentiator Printec sells. Printec should (a) defend Alpha Bank Romania on kiosks and any Siron/AML adjacency, and (b) pitch ANAF/DGRFP centrally on a national counting-machine managed-service framework plus fleet upgrade to displace this RON-hundreds-per-call incumbency with a single framework.
signals.likelihood: Very likely Eutron continues to win the ANAF treasury counting-machine stream call-by-call through 2026-27; a central framework is the only way to break it
signals.followup: Ask Printec Romania whether Eutron has been met in any bank TCR or kiosk bid; obtain Eutron's filed accounts from the Romanian trade register to size it (no figure should be quoted until then).

signals.signal: global/regional payments-infrastructure vendor now embedded in Romania's national rails. Montran is the supplier of the CENTRAL RoPay and Instant Payments solutions, built together with TRANSFOND, and it sells banks connectivity to join the RoPay scheme. Triggers this window: (a) a sole-sourced Banca Nationala a Romaniei contract for payments infrastructure worth RON 477,840 dated 04/05/2026; (b) UniCredit Bank Romania went live with RoPay in its Mobile Banking and Business Mobile apps on 02/02/2026 with Montran named as implementation partner (Montran regional sales director Irina Carcu quoted); (c) Banca Transilvania added new RoPay functionality in BT Pay working with Montran, a partner of 'over 20 years'. TRANSFOND reports roughly 8.8 million users able to transfer by phone number. Note the separate BNR incumbent Wall Street Systems Sweden AB / ION Group (contract 39/P/2026, EUR 2,802,500, 26/05/2026) sits alongside Montran in the same buyer.
signals.source_name: Revista Biz (UniCredit/Montran RoPay) + e-licitatie/BNR contract register via Agent 2
signals.implies: Montran owns the Romanian payments-rail layer that Printec does not sell, but it is the vendor of record inside BNR, BT and UniCredit and is expanding from scheme connectivity into bank-side integration work - the same CIO budget Printec competes for with terminal management (TMS), transaction monitoring (INETCO) and Thales HSM. Printec's realistic play is complementary: pitch INETCO transaction monitoring and Thales payShield HSM around RoPay/instant-payments go-lives at the banks Montran is onboarding, and use RoPay adoption as the reason acquiring/POS estates need refreshed monitoring.
signals.likelihood: High that further Romanian banks go live on RoPay via Montran in the next 6-12 months, each creating an HSM/monitoring attach window
signals.followup: Get the full RoPay participant list from ropay.ro and map which banks have not yet gone live - those are the attach windows for INETCO and Thales HSM.

signals.signal: local-peer, already on the roster but with a materially changed position. On 24/08/2026 EuPlatesc - a BNR-authorised payment institution and one of Romania's main payment processors - announced the first stage of a DIRECT connection to the RoPay infrastructure developed by TRANSFOND, so that merchants can accept RoPay without an intermediary. EuPlatesc had already run Romania's first RoPay transaction at a physical POS terminal in 2025 and subsequently the first live online RoPay transactions with TRANSFOND. This moves EuPlatesc from an e-commerce gateway to a physical-acceptance player wired straight into the national instant-payments rail.
signals.implies: Account-to-account RoPay acceptance at the physical point of sale erodes the card-terminal economics that underpin Printec's Verifone/Castles POS and TMS business in Romania: a merchant who accepts by QR/phone-number needs no card terminal. Printec should position TMS and terminal estates as multi-rail (card + RoPay QR) rather than card-only, and approach acquirers with a terminal-management story that carries RoPay acceptance rather than competing against it.
signals.likelihood: Likely that further RoPay-at-POS integrations follow in the next 6-12 months, compressing terminal demand at the low end
signals.followup: Check whether Verifone and Castles firmware in Romania already supports RoPay QR acceptance; if not, that is a live product gap.

signals.signal: local-peer with national scale. PayPoint Romania ended 2025 with roughly 35% network growth and now operates more than 35,000 assisted POS terminals across Romania, over 75% of which take card payments, processing more than 10.5 million transactions a month (7.2m bill payments, 3.3m card transactions). It has publicly targeted 50,000 active POS by 2028 and is building a Multi-Merchant Partner model plus fintech products positioned as alternatives to bank packages. Separately, on 22/12/2025 PayPoint Romania and Mastercard launched cash WITHDRAWAL at assisted PayPoint POS terminals, capped at RON 500 per transaction in multiples of RON 10, live at over 14,000 partner locations and stated to reach 26,000 points during 2026, explicitly framed as serving villages where 'the nearest ATM is tens of kilometres away'.
signals.source_name: Financiarul.ro / Observator News (PayPoint strategy) + gadget.ro (Mastercard cash-at-POS launch)
signals.implies: Two Printec lines are hit at once. On POS, PayPoint is adding roughly 15,000 assisted terminals by 2028 through a channel Printec does not serve (small retail, rural), squeezing the addressable base for bank-supplied Verifone/Castles estates. On ATM, cash-at-POS at 26,000 rural sites is the cheapest substitute yet for a rural ATM, which weakens the business case for the dispense and intelligent-deposit ATMs Printec sells to Romanian banks. Printec should reframe its Romanian ATM pitch away from rural coverage towards high-value recycling and deposit automation in urban branches, where cash-at-POS cannot compete, and should approach PayPoint itself as a prospective TMS/field-service customer for a 35,000-terminal estate.
signals.likelihood: High - PayPoint has publicly committed to both the 50,000 POS target and the 26,000-location cash-withdrawal rollout
signals.followup: Identify who maintains PayPoint's 35,000-terminal estate today; a national TMS + field-service framework is a legitimate Printec pitch even though PayPoint is a competitor on acceptance.

signals.entity: Global Payments Romania (Global Payments s.r.o. / Erste Bank-BCR joint venture)
signals.signal: global acquirer operating as the de-facto in-house acquiring arm of BCR. Global Payments and BCR, with Visa and Mastercard, launched GP tom, a softPOS application (softPOS = a payment app that turns an ordinary NFC smartphone into a card-acceptance terminal, removing the need for any hardware) working on Android 8+ with an embedded NFC chip, PIN entry required above RON 100. On 29/10/2024 the same joint venture added Tap to Pay on iPhone through GP tom across Romania, the Czech Republic and Austria, distributed to BCR business customers through the George Store, with Global Payments s.r.o. CEO Tomas Furinda quoted. The company markets a dedicated 'oferta POS 2026' terminal campaign. Note: the company's own claimed merchant and terminal counts appear only on a page that returned HTTP 403 to this run, so no figure is asserted here.
signals.implies: [STANDING - dated 2024 for the Tap to Pay step, with a live 2026 POS campaign] BCR is a Printec footprint reference customer on NCR APTRA. Its acquiring is run by a Global Payments joint venture that is now pushing hardware-free acceptance across three Printec countries (Romania, Czechia, Austria), which directly shrinks the Verifone/Castles terminal volume Printec can sell into the BCR merchant base. Printec should protect the BCR relationship on the self-service and APTRA side and pitch terminal management, estate monitoring and field services for the residual attended/unattended hardware Global Payments still needs, rather than competing on terminal supply to small merchants.
signals.likelihood: Certain - GP tom is already live and being marketed in the 2026 POS campaign
signals.followup: Retry globalpayments.ro/oferta-pos-2026 with a desktop browser to capture the 2026 terminal models, pricing and any published merchant/terminal counts.

signals.signal: regional. On 16/07/2026 SIBS Romania announced it had successfully tested POS Sharing on softPOS technology. POS Sharing is SIBS' decade-old Romanian model in which a single physical terminal serves multiple banks; combining it with softPOS lets any smartphone become a shared acceptance point connected to the whole Romanian banking infrastructure. SIBS claims the routing converts up to 90% of transactions from OFF-US to ON-US (i.e. keeps the transaction inside the acquirer's own bank rather than paying an interchange to another), with intelligent transaction routing and optimised processing costs. Target segments named: large retail chains, SMEs, couriers and delivery, street fairs and events, mobile businesses. No merchant or terminal counts were published.
signals.implies: SIBS is attacking the exact economics Printec's POS business rests on: a shared multi-bank terminal already reduced how many physical terminals Romania needs, and moving it to softPOS removes the terminal entirely for the mobile and event segments. Printec should not chase the low-end merchant terminal in Romania; instead sell terminal management (TMS), certification, key management and Thales HSM services to the acquirers and PSPs running these shared/soft estates, and target the attended and unattended hardware segments (kiosks, unattended payment) where a phone cannot substitute.
signals.likelihood: Likely commercial rollout within 6-12 months given the test is complete
signals.followup: Establish which Romanian banks participate in SIBS POS Sharing today and whether SIBS buys terminal hardware or TMS from a third party Printec could displace.

signals.signal: local-peer already on the roster, with a materially changed and much larger position. SelfPay now operates more than 13,000 active self-service Payment Stations in over 3,000 Romanian localities. On 21/05/2026 it reported opening 277 new locations in the first half of May 2026 and a 15% rise in daily national transaction volume, and launched a 'Rapid Transition Program' offering retailers and proximity stores a zero-upfront-investment platform with 300+ services, per-transaction commissions, an OPTIONAL POS TERMINAL for card payments, and included maintenance and technical support. On 03/08/2026 it announced its largest-ever service-portfolio expansion in the SelfPay Now super-app (mobile/connectivity, gaming and gift cards, RCA insurance, vehicle evaluation/ITP/history). SelfPay also pairs with Salt Bank on SelfPay Now and has installed payment machines for CEC Bank.
signals.source_name: HotNews.ro (network expansion) + ZF Comunicate (SelfPay Now portfolio expansion 03/08/2026)
signals.implies: SelfPay is now a 13,000-unit self-service estate that competes with Printec's bank kiosk and self-service line for the same consumer transactions (bill payment, cash deposit to card, tax payment), and its Rapid Transition Program bundles a card POS terminal as a giveaway, which further compresses Printec's small-merchant terminal opportunity. It is also a credible bidder against Printec on public self-service kiosk procurements. Conversely a 13,000-terminal estate is a large managed-services and device-monitoring target: Printec's ATM/device telemetry and field-services proposition maps directly onto it.
signals.likelihood: Continued double-digit network growth through 2026-27 is stated company strategy
signals.followup: Confirm who supplies and services SelfPay's kiosk hardware today, and whether the Salt Bank pairing extends to cash deposit (which would put SelfPay in direct competition with bank recyclers).

signals.signal: local-peer, roster entry materially clarified and expanded. Reported on 23/04/2026: EasyPay, a self-service terminal provider founded in 2010, present in 28 countries, running a network of over 1,100 payment terminals and 15 crypto ATMs, AND OPERATING ITS OWN SELF-SERVICE EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURING FACILITY. 2025 revenue approximately EUR 10 million, roughly 8% growth. It is investing EUR 0.5 million in a digital-reception self-service solution for medical clinics, targeting approximately 100 clinic implementations during 2026 and around 300 within two to three years, claiming up to 60% reduction in reception administrative volume and up to 30% operating-cost optimisation. Sectors covered: retail, hospitality, transport, medical.
signals.implies: A Romanian firm that MANUFACTURES its own kiosks at roughly EUR 10m revenue is a direct low-cost rival to Printec's self-service and bank-kiosk line, and the queue/reception check-in use case it is scaling is the same one Printec sells to bank branches. Printec Romania should expect EasyPay in branch-kiosk and public self-service bids and should differentiate on bank-grade security, cash handling, PCI and multivendor software (x-core) rather than on kiosk price.
signals.likelihood: Likely to appear in Romanian kiosk/self-service bids within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Verify whether this EasyPay is the same legal entity as the roster's existing 'EasyPay' record or a distinct Romanian company; the roster entry needs a registration number.

signals.signal: local-peer, new entrant into the regulated layer. Mobile Distribution, which operates the nearly-30-year-old Un-Doi payment platform, was entered in the BNR register as an authorised PAYMENT INSTITUTION with effect from 15/05/2026, announced 27/05/2026 (authorisation work supported by KPMG Legal and KPMG Advisory). The company states it processes approximately RON 4 billion of transactions a year across a mobile app, over 2,500 payment terminals and more than 11,000 partner retail locations, and has published three strategic directions: expanding the terminal and agent network nationwide, adding new payment functionality now permitted by its payment-institution status, and deepening partner tooling.
signals.implies: A third national self-service/agent payment network (after SelfPay and PayPoint) has just gained the licence it needs to expand terminal-based payment services, which further fragments the Romanian cash-access and bill-payment market away from bank ATMs and weakens the volume case for the dispense/deposit ATMs Printec sells. It is also a fresh 2,500-terminal estate with a stated expansion plan and no publicly named device-management or field-service supplier - a legitimate target for Printec's telemetry, monitoring and managed-services offer.
signals.likelihood: Network expansion is explicit company strategy for the next 6-12 months
signals.followup: Find out who manufactures and services the 2,500 Un-Doi terminals and whether the expansion involves a hardware tender.

signals.signal: local-peer and the Romanian qualified trust service provider (QTSP) that competes head-on with Printec's Namirial digital-onboarding line. certSIGN sells remote video identification audited and certified as equivalent to physical presence under eIDAS, qualified cloud and token e-signature (paperLESS webSIGN), qualified timestamping and long-term preservation, explicitly marketed to banks, insurers, brokers, leasing and factoring firms for onboarding and multi-signer contracting. Fresh triggers from its own newsroom: 21/08/2026 'EUDI Wallet as a mechanism for strong customer authentication (SCA) - a new perspective for the financial-banking sector'; 11/08/2026 qualified e-signature via EUDI Wallet; 24/07/2026 relying-parties obligations under EUDI Wallet; 10/07/2026 certSIGN confirmed interoperability of its solution at ETSI Plugtests 2026; 12/06/2026 all EUDI Wallet interoperability scenarios completed at Moldova Digital Summit 2026; 17/06/2026 a live EUDI Wallet demonstration with Babes-Bolyai University. Separately certSIGN holds a Romanian Ministry of National Defence qualified-trust-services call-off worth RON 2,743,039.32 [STANDING - dated Nov-Dec 2025].
signals.implies: certSIGN is positioning EUDI Wallet as the future authentication and onboarding rail for Romanian banks - the same buying decision Printec addresses with Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC. Because certSIGN is the local QTSP with the certificates, a Romanian bank can source identity, signature and preservation from it directly and never run a separate eKYC tender. Printec Romania should pitch Namirial as the orchestration and journey layer that consumes certSIGN or other QTSP certificates, not as a rival to them, and should bundle it with IMTF Siron AML and FICO so the deal is compliance-wide rather than signature-only.
signals.likelihood: High - EUDI Wallet obligations land across 2026-27 and certSIGN is publishing weekly on the banking angle
signals.followup: Confirm the Namirial-certSIGN relationship (partner or competitor) before Printec Romania approaches a bank on onboarding.

signals.entity: OFFICE HQ SRL (RO32152007), CA.DA GRUPP and Zoopie Solutions (RO45414878)
signals.signal: micro local-peer tail on cash-handling service, surfaced only by the direct-acquisition feed. Alongside Eutron, three further Romanian micro-suppliers took public cash-machine work in 2026: OFFICE HQ SRL won notice DAN2753453 published 12/05/2026 from Municipiul Bacau (R4278337) for 'Mentenanta masini numarat bancnote si piese de schimb' (banknote-counting-machine maintenance plus spare parts) at RON 24,297.78; CA.DA GRUPP took equivalent treasury counting-machine repair calls outside the Cluj region; and Zoopie Solutions sold a single banknote counter to Universitatea de Stiinte (RO14313954) for RON 438.02 under DAN2748025, 05/05/2026. Values are trivial individually but they show the Romanian public cash-equipment estate is serviced by a fragmented set of unbranded local firms with no framework in place.
signals.implies: There is no incumbent framework holder for cash-counting and cash-machine service across the Romanian public sector - work is bought call-by-call at a few hundred RON from whichever local firm answers. That is a structural opening for Printec's managed/field-services line: a single national counting-machine and cash-equipment service framework with ANAF/DGRFP and municipalities would consolidate dozens of micro-awards, and Printec's existing regional field-service organisation is the differentiator none of these firms can match.
signals.likelihood: The fragmented call-by-call pattern will persist through 2026-27 unless a bidder proposes a framework
signals.followup: Draft an unsolicited framework proposition for ANAF/DGRFP national counting-machine managed service and test appetite; check whether Romanian law permits a centralised framework for these below-threshold buys.

signals.entity: EAE Solutions B.V. (Netherlands) and Isitec International (France)
signals.signal: regional/global adjacency competitors in postal and branch automation. EAE Solutions B.V. was awarded a contract covering BOTH Posta Slovenije and C.N. Posta Romana at EUR 6,772,535 against a EUR 6,825,000 estimate, concluded 11/06/2026. Isitec International, a French logistics, postal and general-services automation firm (parcel and mail sorting machines, Isilocker smart lockers, Isitrac 360 track-and-trace, pick-to-light and AGV/AMR), holds three C.N. Posta Romana contracts, the largest at RON 12,425,000 [STANDING - dated 15/05/2025]. Isitec lists Romania among its operating countries. Printec S.I. d.o.o. is the incumbent at Posta Slovenije for parcel-locker supply plus five-year maintenance [STANDING - 2025].
signals.source_name: e-licitatie.ro / Posta Slovenije award records (via Agent 2 tender sweep 27/08/2026)
signals.implies: EAE Solutions has taken a EUR 6.8m award spanning the exact postal buyer where Printec S.I. is the parcel-locker incumbent (Posta Slovenije) and the largest Romanian postal buyer (C.N. Posta Romana), which puts Printec's Slovenian postal-automation renewal at direct risk and shows Printec is not yet on the Romanian postal account. Printec should (a) defend the Posta Slovenije relationship ahead of any re-tender by widening from lockers into branch self-service and cash automation, and (b) use the Slovenian reference to open C.N. Posta Romana, where postal counters are a natural fit for Printec kiosks and cash recyclers.
signals.likelihood: Medium-high that further Posta Romana automation lots come to market within 18 months given three Isitec contracts and the EAE award
signals.followup: Get the exact scope split of the EAE award between Posta Slovenije and Posta Romana, and the end date of Printec S.I.'s Posta Slovenije five-year maintenance so the renewal can be defended early.

signals.entity: Romanian bank in-house acquiring / softPOS wave (ING Bank Romania, OTP Bank Romania, Alpha Bank Romania, CEC Bank, BCR)
signals.signal: bank in-house acquiring teams as competitors, per the Printec competitor-scope rule. Romania's card-acceptance mandate effective 01/01/2026 (reported as OUG/Legea 239/2025) removes the previous RON 50,000 turnover threshold and obliges essentially every entity that collects money from the public - regardless of turnover, legal form, headcount, activity or rural location - to accept modern electronic payments, with ANAF enforcement and fines reported at RON 20,000-50,000. Critically, the law does NOT require a physical terminal: a virtual POS or a mobile app satisfies it. Romanian banks have responded by shipping their own softPOS apps rather than buying terminals - ING SoftPOS, OTP POSibil (Android), Alpha Bank, CEC Bank and BCR (via the Global Payments GP tom app). All figures and the legal reference here come from secondary Romanian legal/press summaries, not from the Monitorul Oficial text, and are flagged Low confidence accordingly.
signals.source_name: StartupCafe (lawyer analysis of the 2026 card-acceptance obligation) and wall-street.ro softPOS coverage
signals.implies: The single biggest expansion of mandated card acceptance in Romanian history is being met with software, not hardware. That is the opposite of a terminal opportunity for Printec's Verifone/Castles line: the new merchants brought in by the mandate will mostly be served by bank softPOS apps, PayPoint, SelfPay and SIBS. Printec's addressable Romanian POS revenue is therefore terminal management (TMS), certification, key injection, PCI/HSM and field services for the acquirers running these mixed soft/hard estates, plus unattended and attended hardware segments a phone cannot serve. Printec should take this to Romanian acquirers as an estate-complexity pitch: five acceptance form factors, one management platform.
signals.likelihood: Already in force; enforcement pressure continues through 2026
signals.followup: Obtain the actual Monitorul Oficial text and article number for the 2026 acceptance obligation before this is used in any Printec commercial material.
